modern:
These words are God’s command to the believer when he is reduced to great straits and brought into extraordinary difficulties. He can’t retreat; he can’t go forward; he is shut in on the right and on the left. What is he to do now? The Master’s word to him is, “Stand still.” It will be good for him if at such times he listens only to his Master’s word, for other, evil advisers come with their suggestions. *Despair* whispers, “Lie down and die; give it all up.” But God wants us to put on a cheerful courage and, even in our worst times, rejoice in his love and faithfulness. *Cowardice* says, “Retreat; go back to the worldling’s way of action; you cannot play the Christian’s part, it is too difficult. Relinquish your principles.” But however hard Satan may press this course on you, you can’t follow it if you are a child of God. His divine command has told you to go from strength to strength, and so you will, and neither death nor hell will turn you from your course. What if for a while you are called to stand still? It is only to renew your strength for some greater advance in due time. *Rash haste* cries, “do something. Stir yourself; to stand still and wait, is sheer idleness.” We *must* be doing something at once (*we* must do it, so we think) instead of looking to the Lord, who will not only do something but will do everything. *Presumption* boasts, “If the sea be before you, march into it and expect a miracle.” But Faith listens neither to Presumption, nor to Despair, nor to Cowardice, nor to Rash Haste; it hears God say, “Stand still,” and it stands as unmovable as a rock.

“*Stand* still”: keep the posture of an upright man, ready for action, expecting further orders, cheerfully and patiently waiting for the voice that directs; and it won’t be long before God says to you, as clearly as Moses said it to the people of Israel, “Go forward.”

modern:
My soul, think about the might of the Lord who is your glory and defense. He is a man of war; Jehovah is his name. All *the forces of heaven* are at his beck and call. Legions wait at his door; cherubim and seraphim, watchers and holy ones, principalities and powers are all attentive to his will. If our eyes weren’t blinded by the eye disease of the flesh, we would see horses of fire and chariots of fire all around the Lord’s dear people. *The powers of nature* are all under the absolute control of the Creator. Stormy wind and tempest, lightning and rain, snow and hail, the soft dews and the cheering sunshine come and go at his command. He loosens the bands of Orion and binds the sweet influences of the Pleiades. Earth, sea and air, and the places under the earth, are the barracks of Jehovah’s great armies; space is his camping ground, light is his banner, and flame is his sword. When he goes out to war, famine ravages the land, plague strikes the nations, hurricane sweeps the sea, tornado shakes the mountains, and earthquake makes the solid world tremble. As for *living creatures*, they all acknowledge his rule. From the great fish that swallowed the prophet, down to the “all manner of flies” that plagued the field of Zoan, all are his servants; like the palmerworm, the caterpillar and the cankerworm, they are squadrons of his great army, for his camp is very great.

My soul, make sure you are at peace with this mighty King. Yes, more: be sure to enlist under his banner, for to fight against him is madness, and to serve him is glory. Jesus, Immanuel, God with us, is ready to receive recruits for the army of the Lord. If I haven’t enlisted already, let me go to him before I sleep and beg to be accepted through his merits; and if I already am, as I hope I am, a soldier of the cross, let me take heart, for the enemy is powerless compared with my Lord, whose camp is very great.

modern: In fighting certain sins there is no way to win but by running away. The old writers on nature wrote a great deal about basilisks, whose eyes fascinated their prey and made them easy victims; in the same way, merely gazing at wickedness puts us in grave danger. Whoever wants to be safe from doing evil must hurry away from the occasions of it. We must make a covenant with our eyes not even to look at what tempts us, for such sins need only a spark to start, and a blaze follows in an instant. Who would recklessly walk into a leper colony and sleep among its horrible decay? Only someone who wanted to be a leper himself would court infection like that. If a sailor knew how to avoid a storm, he would do anything rather than risk trying to ride it out. Careful pilots have no wish to see how close to the quicksand they can sail, or how often they can touch a rock without springing a leak; their aim is to keep as near as possible to the middle of a safe channel.

Today I may be exposed to great danger. Let me have the serpent’s wisdom to keep out of it and avoid it. The wings of a dove may be more use to me today than the jaws of a lion. It’s true I may seem to lose by turning down evil company, but I had better leave my cloak than lose my character. It isn’t necessary for me to be rich, but it is essential for me to be pure. No ties of friendship, no chains of beauty, no flashes of talent, no arrows of ridicule must turn me from the wise decision to run from sin. The devil I am to resist, and he will run from me; but the lusts of the flesh *I* must run from, or they will surely overcome me. O God of holiness, keep your Josephs safe, so that Madam Bubble doesn’t bewitch them with her vile suggestions. May the horrible trinity of the world, the flesh and the devil never overcome us!

modern:
Losses and hardships are often the means the great Shepherd uses to bring his wandering sheep home; like fierce dogs, they harry the wanderers back to the fold. There is no taming lions if they are too well fed. They must be brought down from their great strength, and their stomachs must be lowered, and then they will submit to the tamer’s hand. We have often seen the Christian made obedient to the Lord’s will by scarcity of bread and hard work. When they are rich and well supplied with goods, many who profess the faith carry their heads much too high and talk very boastfully. Like David, they flatter themselves: “My mountain standeth fast; I shall never be moved.”

When the Christian grows wealthy, has a good name, good health and a happy family, he too often lets Mr. Carnal Security feast at his table; and then, if he is a true child of God, a rod is being prepared for him. Wait a while, and perhaps you will see his property melt away like a dream. There goes part of his estate; how quickly the acres change hands! That debt, that unpaid bill: how fast his losses pour in! Where will they end? It is a blessed sign of divine life if, when these embarrassments come one after another, he begins to be distressed about his backsliding and takes himself off to his God. Blessed are the waves that wash the sailor onto the rock of salvation! Losses in business are often made holy, to enrich our souls. If the chosen soul won’t come to the Lord with full hands, it will come with empty ones. If God, in his grace, finds no other way to make us honor him among men, he will throw us into the deep; if we fail to honor him on the pinnacle of riches, he will bring us into the valley of poverty. Yet don’t lose heart, heir of sorrow, when you are rebuked like this. Recognize instead the loving hand that disciplines you, and say, “I will arise, and go unto my Father.”
